narrative:
Your loan application was reviewed carefully, and unfortunately, we were unable to approve it at this time. Based on the information provided, the system predicted a 56% likelihood that the loan could pose a higher risk of repayment difficulties. While this doesn’t mean you’re unable to manage credit, it does suggest that certain aspects of your financial profile raised concerns compared to others who were approved.

The most significant factor in this decision was your credit history. While it’s positive that you’ve either never taken out a loan before or have paid off all past debts, this also means there’s no track record of successfully managing ongoing credit obligations. Most approved applicants have a history of existing loans that were repaid on time, which gives lenders more confidence in their ability to handle new debt.

Another key concern was the current balance in your checking account. Having less than 200 DM available—especially when no other applicants with similar balances were approved—suggests limited financial flexibility to handle unexpected expenses or loan payments. A stronger checking account balance is often seen as a buffer against temporary financial setbacks.

On a more positive note, the amount you requested—4,280 DM—was actually a factor working in your favor, as it’s closer to what many approved applicants borrow. However, this alone wasn’t enough to offset the other concerns.

To improve your chances in the future, focusing on building a stronger credit history—perhaps by responsibly managing a smaller credit line—and increasing your checking account balance could make a meaningful difference. Additionally, since your requested loan term of 30 months is longer than the average approved term of 19 months, opting for a shorter repayment period might also help. We encourage you to review these areas and consider reapplying when your financial situation has strengthened.
